### Project Name

Agent Plugins

### Project Description

Agent Plugins is an open, vendor-neutral standard for packaging reusable components that extend AI agents into distributable plugins. A common directory format lets plugin authors package Agent Skills and MCP server configurations for use across compatible clients. Client-owned extension namespaces accommodate capabilities outside the portable core.

The project grew out of earlier Open Plugin work and is now maintained by a cross-vendor Technical Steering Committee. [Specification 1.0.0](https://github.com/agentplugins/agent-plugins-spec/blob/main/spec/1.0.0.md) is published; 1.1.0 is a working draft. The project includes the specification and JSON schemas, documentation, a reference plugin with a migration skill, and a client conformance suite. [Project overview](https://github.com/agentplugins/agent-plugins-spec), [maintainer roster](https://github.com/agentplugins/agent-plugins-spec/blob/main/MAINTAINERS.md).

### Alignment with AAIF Mission

Agent Plugins supports interoperability between agent clients through a small, vendor-neutral packaging contract. Authors can distribute reusable skills and MCP configuration together, while clients retain control of their product experience, policy, and extensions. A shared package format reduces the need to duplicate common components across vendor-specific formats.

This complements AAIF’s goals for open, community-driven agent infrastructure, interoperability, and developer workflows. [Agent Plugins overview](https://agent-plugins.org/).

### Relation to Existing AAIF Projects

Agent Plugins complements Model Context Protocol, an AAIF project, by defining the package configuration used to discover and connect to MCP servers. MCP remains authoritative for its wire behavior and lifecycle semantics; Agent Plugins defines packaging and client configuration.

Agent Plugins also incorporates the separately maintained Agent Skills format, which has [been proposed for contribution to AAIF](https://github.com/aaif/project-proposals/issues/47). Agent Plugins defines discovery of skills within a plugin, while Agent Skills remains authoritative for the skill format. [Specification §§7.1–7.2](https://github.com/agentplugins/agent-plugins-spec/blob/main/spec/1.0.0.md#7-component-types).

### Example Use Cases and Evidence of Adoption

Use cases include distributing reusable task instructions as skills, bundling local or remote MCP server configuration alongside those skills, and migrating an existing client-specific package to a portable core while retaining client extensions. The [canonical example](https://github.com/agentplugins/agent-plugins-example) includes a migration skill illustrating that workflow.

Agent Plugins support has shipped in VS Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, ChatGPT & Codex, Kiro, Hermes Agent, OpenClaw, Grok Bot, NanoClaw, and OpenHands. [Compatible clients](https://agent-plugins.org/compatible-clients).

Direct client documentation describes support for the format:

- [VS Code](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/agent-customization/agent-plugins)
- [Cursor](https://cursor.com/docs/plugins)
- [GitHub Copilot](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/agents/about-plugins)
- [ChatGPT/Codex packaging guide](https://developers.openai.com/plugins/build/plugins)
- [Kiro](https://kiro.dev/docs/powers/)
- [Hermes Agent](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/developer-guide/plugins)
- [OpenClaw](https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/bundles)
- [NanoClaw](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/blob/main/docs/templates.md)
- [OpenHands](https://docs.openhands.dev/overview/agent-plugins)

### Technical Committee Sponsor (if identified)

None identified.

### GitHub Repository URL

https://github.com/agentplugins/agent-plugins-spec

### License

Apache-2.0 for software and schemas; CC-BY-4.0 for specification text and documentation; MIT for the example repository. Third-party materials retain their original licenses.

### Governance Model

The project is governed by its [Technical Charter](https://github.com/agentplugins/agent-plugins-spec/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md). Its TSC consists of the Core Maintainers and Lead Core Maintainer. Roles are held by individuals; seats are not permanently reserved for companies, and no vendor may control a majority of Core Maintainer seats.

The TSC oversees the specification, release and compatibility policy, contribution workflows, conformance tooling, and technical disputes. The charter defines promotion, removal, voting, and amendment rules.

### CI/CD & Release Workflow

Specification 1.0.0 is published with corresponding versioned schemas and a [v1.0.0 Git tag](https://github.com/agentplugins/agent-plugins-spec/tree/v1.0.0). The specification requires new releases for schema changes and prohibits reassigning published schema identifiers. Specification 1.1.0 remains a working draft. [Versioning rules](https://github.com/agentplugins/agent-plugins-spec/blob/main/spec/1.0.0.md#10-versioning).

The [conformance suite](https://github.com/agentplugins/agent-plugins-conformance) has GitHub Actions CI covering checks and tests on Ubuntu and Windows with Node.js 22 and 24, plus a pinned native Codex smoke test on both operating systems. The smoke test collects MCP observations and retains reports and diagnostics as artifacts. It does not run a model turn or certify whole-client conformance. [CI workflow](https://github.com/agentplugins/agent-plugins-conformance/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml), [suite README](https://github.com/agentplugins/agent-plugins-conformance/blob/main/README.md).

The suite’s [release policy](https://github.com/agentplugins/agent-plugins-conformance/blob/main/docs/release-policy.md) defines independent suite versions, exact specification targets, immutable release contents, and annotated release tags.

The [documentation site](https://github.com/agentplugins/agent-plugins-site/blob/main/README.md) builds with Next.js and publishes documentation and canonical schemas at [agent-plugins.org](http://agent-plugins.org).

Specification releases have no fixed cadence. The TSC agrees to a release, the specification is frozen and tagged, and supporting repositories such as the documentation site and conformance suite are updated. Supporting-repository changes may be prepared concurrently in separate branches.

### Public-Facing Contribution Process for Specifications

The public [contribution guide](https://github.com/agentplugins/agent-plugins-spec/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) directs material feature or behavior proposals to GitHub Discussions first. Proposals describe a concrete interoperability need and identify implementers prepared to adopt the behavior. Bugs use GitHub Issues; small editorial corrections may be submitted directly as pull requests.

Changes to the portable contract must update the relevant prose, schemas, examples, identifiers, references, and conformance checklist together. Pull requests describe the resulting contract, link the preceding discussion or issue, and identify validation performed.

### Publicly Accessible Issue Tracker

[Specification issues](https://github.com/agentplugins/agent-plugins-spec/issues) and [specification discussions](https://github.com/agentplugins/agent-plugins-spec/discussions). Supporting repositories also have public issue trackers.

### External Project Dependencies

The portable contract depends on the separately maintained [Agent Skills specification](https://agentskills.io/specification) and [MCP specification](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification). Agent Skills is [Apache-2.0-licensed](https://github.com/agentskills/agentskills/blob/main/LICENSE). MCP’s [current licensing notice](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/blob/main/LICENSE) describes a transition from MIT to Apache-2.0 for code/specifications, with documentation under CC-BY-4.0 and some earlier contributions remaining MIT.

The [schemas](https://github.com/agentplugins/agent-plugins-spec/tree/main/schemas/1.0.0) use JSON Schema draft 2020-12; the JSON Schema specification repository offers [BSD-3-Clause or AFL-3.0 licensing](https://github.com/json-schema-org/json-schema-spec#license).

The conformance development package uses [MCP TypeScript SDK, Ajv, and esbuild](https://github.com/agentplugins/agent-plugins-conformance/blob/main/package.json). The pinned bundled SDK and Ajv license notices are MIT; esbuild is [MIT-licensed](https://github.com/evanw/esbuild/blob/main/LICENSE.md). Bundled dependency licenses are recorded in [third-party notices](https://github.com/agentplugins/agent-plugins-conformance/blob/main/plugins/agent-plugins-conformance-core/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md), including MIT and ISC material.

The documentation site’s [direct dependencies and development tools](https://github.com/agentplugins/agent-plugins-site/blob/main/package.json) use the following licenses:

- **MIT:** `@icons-pack/react-simple-icons`, `@vercel/analytics`, `clsx`, `cmdk`, `fumadocs-core`, `fumadocs-mdx`, `fumadocs-ui`, `mermaid`, `next`, `next-themes`, `radix-ui`, `react`, `react-dom`, `react-player`, `shiki`, `sonner`, `tailwind-merge`, `vaul`, `zod`, `@tailwindcss/postcss`, `@types/mdx`, `@types/node`, `@types/react`, `@types/react-dom`, `postcss`, `tailwindcss`, and `tw-animate-css`.
- **Apache-2.0:** `@vercel/speed-insights`, `class-variance-authority`, and `typescript`.
- **ISC, with MIT terms for Feather-derived portions:** `lucide-react`. [Lucide license](https://github.com/lucide-icons/lucide/blob/main/LICENSE).
- **Bundled artwork:** the React Simple Icons wrapper is MIT, while its bundled Simple Icons artwork is [CC0-1.0](https://github.com/simple-icons/simple-icons/blob/16.12.0/LICENSE.md).

Affiliations identify the organizations represented in specification discussions; governance roles belong to the individuals.

All five Core Maintainers have write access to the specification repository. GitHub records thirteen human commit contributors across the project repositories, including predecessor history.

### Leadership Team & Decision Process

The five Core Maintainers above form the TSC; Jonathan Hefner is Lead Core Maintainer and TSC Chair under the charter’s default rule.

The project seeks consensus. Each TSC member has one vote. Quorum is 50%; ordinary decisions require a majority of those present, and electronic votes require a majority of all members. The Lead Core Maintainer serves as technical tie-breaker when consensus fails. Charter amendments require two-thirds of the entire TSC. [Charter §§2, 5, 7, 11](https://github.com/agentplugins/agent-plugins-spec/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md).

### Roadmap

The next planned release is [Agent Plugins v1.1.0](https://github.com/agentplugins/agent-plugins-spec/milestone/1).

Portable Hooks support is the planned headline feature. Its design is being incubated and has not yet been adopted.

The public milestone also contains proposals for display names and icons, namespaced skill discovery, regex-portable validation, stricter handling of malformed extensions, and per-server MCP extension data. These proposals remain open.

We plan to release v1.1 after Hooks is finalized and a brief grace period has elapsed. No release date has been set.

### Security

The published specification defines package-path containment, local selection of supported schemas during loading, and a prohibition on embedding credentials in MCP environment configuration. These requirements govern the package contract; they do not sandbox subprocesses. [Specification §§4.1, 5.2, 9.2](https://github.com/agentplugins/agent-plugins-spec/blob/main/spec/1.0.0.md).

The conformance suite provides evidence for covered behaviors and explicitly documents its [coverage limits](https://github.com/agentplugins/agent-plugins-conformance/blob/main/docs/coverage-limits.md).

### Additional Information

The Agent Plugins TSC has unanimously approved pursuing contribution of the project to AAIF. Jonathan Hefner is coordinating the application as TSC lead.

**Preferred initial lifecycle stage: Growth.** The project has shipped implementations across independent vendors and a TSC spanning five organizations. Its next planned specification release is v1.1, with portable Hooks support as the headline feature.

Supporting repositories: [documentation site](https://github.com/agentplugins/agent-plugins-site), [example plugin](https://github.com/agentplugins/agent-plugins-example), [conformance suite](https://github.com/agentplugins/agent-plugins-conformance), and [organization profile](https://github.com/agentplugins/.github).
